clue.text: Full up inside

parts.note: a plain description of how a stomach feels after a big meal, filled to the top within

explanation.surface: Someone pats their belly after a feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Having eaten as much as one can hold is to be sated, with nothing more wanted.

clue.text: Prunella her own MD

definitions.meaning: Prunella is the botanical genus of a common herb once used for healing wounds
a doctor who treats herself, as in 'physician, heal thyself'

explanation.surface: A woman named Prunella is her own doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prunella' looks like a woman's name but is the plant genus Prunella vulgaris.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant Prunella vulgaris earned its common name as a wound remedy, and treating oneself is curing oneself.

clue.text: These little cats are great!

parts.note: small young animals that belong to the big cats, which are called the great cats

explanation.surface: Someone enthuses about some kittens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great' reads as praise, but the 'great cats' are lions, leopards and their kin, so these little ones are the young of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Young striped big cats are small felines from the family of great cats.

clue.text: Scent a rat, terriers ? The reverse

indicators.note: The reverse tells us to read the run of the pieces just given from back to front

parts.note: taken as written
Terriers was the nickname for members of the Territorial Army, TA

explanation.surface: Dogs sniff out a rat, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: Terriers were soldiers of the Territorial Army (TA), Britain's volunteer reserve; 'The reverse' turns RATTA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Attar is a fragrant essential oil pressed from rose petals, a perfume.

clue.text: Recipient of divine footwear, one of the 5 suggests

definitions.text: Recipient of divine footwear, one of the 5 suggests

parts.words: Recipient of divine footwear, one of the 5 suggests
parts.note: the 5 are the songs of 5 Across; one says God will cast out his shoe over a neighbouring land, so a native of it gets the shoe

explanation.surface: Someone receives heavenly shoes, as a famous song implies.
explanation.walkthrough: Psalms 60 and 108 have 'over Edom will I cast out my shoe', so a person of Edom receives God's thrown shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Edom, the land south-east of the Dead Sea, an enemy of Israel in the Bible.

clue.text: The underwritten donations for certain songs

parts.note: PS, the postscript, is the part written underneath a letter's signature
alms are gifts given to the poor

explanation.surface: Insured charitable gifts are earmarked for a particular set of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underwritten' looks like insurance, but here it is the postscript, the bit literally written under a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical psalms are sacred songs or hymns, a particular kind of song.

clue.text: So frigid-looking a lass attracted little company

definitions.text: So frigid-looking a lass attracted little company

parts.words: So frigid-looking a lass attracted little company
parts.note: a fairy-tale girl, pale as fresh-fallen flakes, who lived with seven dwarfs, a company of little men

explanation.surface: A cold-looking girl had few friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attracted little company' reads as 'was lonely', but the company was little in size: the seven dwarfs of the fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale princess was named for skin as pale as snow, and kept house for seven dwarfs.

clue.text: Saint noted for moving mounts

parts.note: a famous horse race at Doncaster, so a 'saint' known for horses running

explanation.surface: A holy man was famed for shifting mountains by faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Leger is a classic English flat race at Doncaster; 'moving mounts' sounds like faith moving mountains but means galloping horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The St Leger Stakes, the oldest English classic horse race, bears this name after its saint-like prefix.

clue.text: The strain after being on the motorway Missis ?

indicators.note: after being on means once a piece has been taken off, the remainder is what is left behind

parts.note: missis is the old spoken form of mistress, the woman of the house
the M1 was Britain's first motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A wife is under pressure after driving on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1, London to Yorkshire, was Britain's first motorway; take MI off the front of MISTRESS (what 'Missis' stands for) and STRESS is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure or tension is a strain, physical or mental.

clue.text: Rightly clever

definitions.meaning: read as two French words, 'to the right', so in a right-handed or proper way

explanation.surface: Someone is clever in the proper way.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from French à droit, 'to the right', so read as two words it means 'rightly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft and skilful with hand or mind, from the French for right-handed dexterity.

clue.text: Balsa, Boffin's solicitor ?

definitions.meaning: balsa is a very light timber, used for model aircraft
in Dickens's Our Mutual Friend, Mortimer ... is the lawyer who acts for Mr Boffin

explanation.surface: A scientist's lawyer is made of flimsy wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boffin' looks like British slang for a scientist, but it is Mr Boffin, the Golden Dustman of Dickens's Our Mutual Friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is the classic timber of low weight, and Dickens named Boffin's lawyer Mortimer Lightwood.

clue.text: Urban area of Kensington Gardens

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the place is found as a run of letters inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A city district is part of a well-known London park.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Urban' alone as the definition with 'area of' as indicator, but an adjective cannot stand for a town; 'Urban area' is the definition and 'of' signals the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Ongar is a small town in Essex, a built-up place and so an urban area.

clue.text: Letter-payer

parts.note: a letter here is one who lets property; the person who pays such a landlord is the one renting

explanation.surface: Someone pays for a letter, like postage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' reads as something posted, but here it is one who lets out property, and the clue describes the tenant who pays them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rents goods or premises pays the owner who lets them out.

clue.text: Plant that should not get the rust

definitions.text: Plant that should not get the rust

parts.words: Plant that should not get the rust
parts.note: plant is a factory, and one dealing in a metal that corrodes ought, ironically, to be kept from corroding

explanation.surface: A gardener worries about a fungal disease on a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' and 'rust' suggest a garden and the fungal disease of leaves; the plant is a factory and the rust is corrosion of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory where metal is smelted or forged is a works for that metal, which is prone to corrosion.

clue.text: A vehicle I have taken-from Billingsgate ?

definitions.note: Billingsgate fish market was famous for its porters' foul language, so billingsgate means coarse abuse

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone boards a bus that has come from a London fish market.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate was London's fish market, whose porters were notorious for swearing, so 'billingsgate' became a word for foul language.
explanation.definitionFit: Language of the fish-market kind is coarse and insulting, the speech of a foul-mouthed person.

clue.text: Lively kid, unmannerly, not without love, rash

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
unmannerly means rude

indicators.note: without tells us to remove the following letter from the word before it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A badly behaved child is reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes O (love, zero in tennis) from NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting hastily without thought for consequences is unwise and hasty.

clue.text: Sad as Sibelius in the gay whirl

definitions.meaning: a French word for melancholy, used in English too

definitions.text: as Sibelius in the gay whirl
definitions.meaning: Sibelius wrote the Valse ..., and a valse or waltz is a whirling dance

explanation.surface: A composer is gloomy in the middle of a merry dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gay whirl' is a waltz, French valse: Sibelius's best-known short piece is Valse Triste, the 'sad waltz'.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word means melancholy or mournful, as in Sibelius's sad waltz.

clue.text: Brains trust adapting caterpillars to war ?

definitions.text: Brains trust adapting caterpillars to war

parts.words: Brains trust adapting caterpillars to war
parts.note: a group of experts, read as an armoured vehicle on caterpillar tracks that thinks

explanation.surface: Experts study how insect larvae might be used in warfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caterpillars' are tracked vehicles, which in war became armoured tanks; a 'brains trust' is a panel of experts.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of experts gathered to generate ideas and policy, a group of brains.

clue.text: The painter, young fellow, is at the stern!

definitions.note: read as 'the one who is at the stern'

parts.note: David Cox was an English landscape painter
a swain is a country youth or lover

explanation.surface: A boat's rope and a young lad are at the back of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painter' suggests the rope that ties up a boat, which fits 'stern', but here it is David Cox, English watercolourist.
explanation.definitionFit: The helmsman of a rowing boat sits in the stern, steering and setting the stroke.

clue.text: One equally leggy

parts.note: iso- means equal and -pod means foot, so a creature whose legs are all alike

explanation.surface: Someone is just as long-legged as another.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is Greek: iso- 'equal' and pod- 'foot', for crustaceans such as woodlice whose legs are all of similar size.
explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean order, including woodlice, has seven pairs of similar walking limbs.

clue.text: A dike as time goes on requires repair

parts.note: a dike is a bank or dam holding water back
age is time passing, as in growing old

explanation.surface: An old sea wall needs mending over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: harm is what calls for mending.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm done to something is what needs fixing afterwards.

clue.text: In Italy a voter is so confused

indicators.note: so confused says the letters just named are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: An Italian voter is bewildered by the choice.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging VOTERIS gives the answer; 'In Italy' defines a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Treviso is a city in the Veneto region of north-east Italy.

clue.text: No agent misrepresented the vessel's capacity

indicators.note: misrepresented says the letters of the words before are presented wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: No shipping agent lied about how much the ship could carry.
explanation.definitionFit: The cargo a ship can hold is measured in tons.

clue.text: New Latin American province

parts.note: the Canadian province of Nova ..., Latin for New Scotland; the clue's 'New' gives the first half

explanation.surface: A region of Latin America has been newly formed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin American' suggests South America, but read 'New Latin' (nova) plus this word as the name of a North American province, Nova Scotia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin name for Scotland, completing Nova Scotia, the Canadian province.

clue.text: Pass our chap to the paint-dealer

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Hand our man over to the paint shop owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like a verb (hand over) but is a noun: a col is a pass between mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: An old trade name for a seller of artists' paints and pigments.

clue.text: Harris get your gun

definitions.meaning: ... and Harris form one island in the Outer Hebrides
a First World War machine gun

explanation.surface: Someone tells Harris to fetch a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harris' looks like a man's name but is the southern part of the island of Lewis and Harris, in Scotland's Outer Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern part of the Hebridean island shared with Harris, and a light machine gun of the Great War.

clue.text: Goes without a hitch ?

parts.note: goes on foot rather than hitching a lift, not 'goes smoothly'

explanation.surface: Everything goes smoothly, with no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a hitch' normally means smoothly; here a hitch is a hitched lift, so the traveller walks.
explanation.definitionFit: Long walks in the country are taken on foot, not by thumbing rides.

clue.text: Dauphin in disguise arrested before he can get in

definitions.text: arrested before he can get in

indicators.note: disguise says the letters are scrambled once the little word in is taken out of them

explanation.surface: A French prince in a costume is caught before he can enter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguise' looks like part of the French prince's costume; 'had up' is British slang for brought before a court after arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought before the magistrates after being arrested, charged.

clue.text: Terrible waste of leather could be painful

definitions.text: Terrible waste of leather could be painful

indicators.note: terrible says the letters of the next word are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Wasting good leather would be a painful thing to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrambling WASTE gives the Scottish schoolteacher's leather strap, so the whole clue also describes it: a terrible strip of leather that hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish leather strap with split ends, once used to punish pupils on the hand.

clue.text: Top of the Pops ?

parts.note: Pops are fathers, and the one above a father in the family tree is his own father

explanation.surface: The name of a chart of hit records.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like the BBC's pop-music chart show; read Pops as dads, and the one at the top is the father's father.
explanation.definitionFit: A father's father is a grandfather, the senior dad above the other dads.

clue.text: They are disposable as lots

parts.note: lots at an auction are sets of items

explanation.surface: Items are thrown away in batches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposable' reads as throwaway, but means available for disposal or use, as property is.
explanation.definitionFit: Property and resources one owns can be sold or used, so they are at one's disposal.

clue.text: Engaged by word of mouth

parts.note: booked or reserved in advance, and the word contains spoken, uttered aloud

explanation.surface: A couple got betrothed with a spoken promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' suggests betrothal; the sense is ordered or reserved, and the word itself has 'spoken' in it, matching 'by word of mouth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordered or reserved beforehand, as a made-to-measure suit is ordered.
